summary: Syrian-style labneh, adapted from Poopa Dweck's Aromas of Aleppo: 1 quart of thick yogurt drained overnight in cheesecloth, mixed with cumin, dried spearmint, Aleppo pepper and salt, rolled into balls and served in olive oil.
glance: 1 quart thick Greek-style (or 1.5 quarts thinner natural yogurt)
overnight in the refrigerator, in a double layer of cheesecloth
cumin, dried spearmint, Aleppo pepper or chili flakes, sea salt
faq: What is labneh?

Labneh, also spelled lebneh, is eaten all over the Middle East. The name covers yogurt-based products from very thick liquid to a firmly pressed fresh cheese. It's made by draining the liquid from plain yogurt through cheesecloth and optionally adding flavorings.
What yogurt should I use?

A good one, such as Fage or Greek Gods. The author used full fat, thinks 2% will be fine too, and hasn't tried non-fat. Use 1 quart of thick Greek-style yogurt or 1.5 quarts of thinner natural yogurt.
How do I drain the yogurt?

Line a colander with a double layer of cheesecloth set in a bowl, pour in the yogurt and tie the cheesecloth into a ball, ideally suspended from a wooden spoon over the colander rim so its weight helps it drain. Refrigerate overnight with enough room in the bowl to catch the liquid.
How firm should the labneh be?
Firm enough to form somewhat decent balls. If not, drain it more.
How do I serve it?

Mix in the cumin, spearmint, pepper and salt, form balls a bit smaller than a golf ball with greased hands, arrange in a shallow bowl with about 1/8 inch of olive oil, and garnish with parsley or cilantro. Serve with toasted pita.
What can I use instead of Aleppo pepper?
Red chili flakes are a decent substitute.

summary: Chana dal in the style of the Puri Jagannath Temple: split chickpeas and red lentils simmered until almost tender, cooked 20 more minutes with a pureed coconut and sweet spice paste, then finished with a butter-fried tempering of cumin, mustard, fennel and fenugreek.
glance: 4 as a main course with rice, or 8 as a side dish
simmer until almost tender, then 20 more minutes with the spice paste
fry mustard, cumin, fennel and fenugreek about 1 minute
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you use oil instead of butter
yield: 4 as a main course with rice, or 8 as a side dish
faq: What is chana dal?

The split, small brown chickpeas with their seed coats removed. They cook much more quickly than normal chickpeas but keep a bit of integrity and texture instead of falling apart. Find them at any Indian grocery or at Whole Foods.
What does dal mean?
Dal is the Indian word for the whole range of dried beans and lentils, and also the name of a soup or thick stew made from them.
What is tempering?

Frying spices in a bit of oil or ghee and adding them to a dish at the last minute so you can fully appreciate their volatile compounds. Here the sweeter spices (cinnamon, cloves, coriander) go in early and the pungent ones (mustard, fennel, cumin, fenugreek) go in at the last minute.
Can I mix in red lentils?
The author only had 1.5 cups of chana dal and made up the difference with red lentils, which dissolve and create a sauce around the chana dal.
How do I adjust the texture?
Cook it a little longer for a thicker, stew-like consistency, or add more water for a thinner soup.
What do you serve with chana dal?
Basmati rice and plain yogurt or raita for a one-pot meal, or use it as a side dish in a more elaborate feast.

summary: West African-style eggplant and okra stew with ginger and black pepper: golf-ball-sized eggplants roasted about 30 minutes at 400°F, then added to okra, summer squash and tomatoes simmered 15 minutes, with corn and fresh ginger stirred in at the end.
glance: 8 very small (about 1 1/2 pounds total), roasted at 400°F about 30 minutes
faq: What eggplant do you use for this stew?

Tiny eggplants just a bit bigger than a golf ball, which you may find at a farmer's market in late summer or a store that specializes in Thai or Indian ingredients. Otherwise use a regular globe eggplant cut into bite-sized pieces.
How do you cook the eggplant?
Prick each with a fork and roast on a sheet pan at 400 degrees until completely tender, about 30 minutes. Cut non-golf-ball eggplant into bite-sized pieces first.
How do I make the stew richer?
Mix 1/2 cup of unsweetened peanut butter or sunflower butter into the broth, or add 1/2 cup of shelled, roasted peanuts.
When do I add the corn and ginger?
Two minutes before serving, add the corn kernels and the remaining tablespoon of fresh ginger.
What do you serve with it?
Serve it over a bowl of rice for a satisfying one-dish meal.

summary: "Caviar" (beluga) black lentil salad with a sherry vinegar dressing, arugula, crispy fried shallots, cherry tomatoes and toast spread with roasted garlic; lentils simmer about 25 minutes and garlic roasts about 30 minutes at 350°F.
glance: 1 1/4 cups black (beluga or "caviar") lentils, about 25 minutes
sherry vinegar and extra-virgin olive oil

summary: Peperonata to serve over polenta: 8 bell peppers roasted about 40 minutes at 400°F, peeled and stewed with a "cheater sofrito" of pureed onion, garlic and tomato paste, red onion and sherry vinegar for about 15 minutes.
glance: 8 bell peppers, roasted about 40 minutes at 400°F
pureed onion and garlic browned, then tomato paste cooked about 10 minutes
Vegetarian, gluten-free, kosher and optionally vegan
faq: What is sofrito?

A long-cooked sauce of onions, garlic and tomatoes in Spain. The same basic method is used in many countries with variations; in Cuba it would have green bell peppers, and elsewhere in the Caribbean annatto and pork.
What is cheater sofrito?

This recipe's version uses tomato paste instead of whole tomatoes, which gives a huge head start on removing the liquid and getting browned flavors. You can double or quadruple the sofrito and freeze leftovers.
How do you roast the peppers?

Cut the tops and bottoms off, halve vertically, remove seeds and ribs, place cut-side down on a rimmed baking sheet at 400°F until well blistered, about 40 minutes. Cool in a covered bowl, peel, and tear into strips, saving all the liquid.
What pan should I use?
A large non-reactive skillet: not cast iron, and not non-stick.
How should I make the polenta?
The author likes the basic pressure cooker method from Hip Pressure Cooking, finished with plenty of grated Parmesan, milk and butter. A more traditional stovetop method also works.
Is peperonata vegan?
It is vegetarian, gluten-free, kosher and optionally vegan, depending on how you serve it.

summary: Vietnamese salad rolls (goi cuon) with shiso and tofu: rice paper wrappers filled with shiso, mint, cilantro, rice vermicelli, cucumber, carrot and pan-fried tofu, served with a lime, ginger, lemongrass and sweet chili dipping sauce; makes 12 rolls.
glance: 12 rolls; two per person is a good appetizer, three a light lunch
Prep 1 hr, cook 20 min, total 1 hr 20 min
12 rice paper wrappers (banh trang), softened in very hot water for a few seconds
faq: What rice paper do I need for salad rolls?
The kind that says banh trang on the package and isn't flavored with anything like sesame.
How do you soften the rice paper wrappers?
Submerge one wrapper in a shallow pan of very hot water for just a few seconds. It will still be fairly firm when you remove it, but it continues to hydrate while you arrange the ingredients.
How do you roll Vietnamese salad rolls?

Layer shiso, mint and cilantro near the edge closest to you, add a small amount of rice noodles (less than you think), put cucumber and carrot in a line near the center and two pieces of tofu near the far edge. Roll around the herbs and noodles, tuck, fold in the edges like a burrito, then continue rolling with firm but not bursting pressure.
Is this a weeknight recipe?
Probably not for a busy family with young kids. Allow a fair amount of time to prep and roll, and expect it to take a few tries to roll neatly; even the failures will be delicious.
Why use shiso?
This version uses shiso instead of lettuce for a more pronounced and complex herbal flavor.
What dipping sauce goes with them?
A sweet chili sauce with lime, ginger, garlic, lemongrass and green onion. A more traditional peanut and hoisin sauce also works.

summary: Apricot and sweet onion mostarda: apricots simmered 15 minutes with sugar, sherry vinegar, Dijon, coriander, fennel and ginger, pureed and strained, then simmered 15 more minutes with diced sweet onion until thick like pickle relish; yields about 1 cup.
glance: 15 minutes, puree and strain, then about 15 more minutes with the onion
Vegetarian, vegan and potentially gluten-free (check the prepared ingredients)
faq: What is mostarda?

Mostarda di frutta is an unusual Italian condiment, made most famously in Cremona, with a complex mixture of sweet and sour, fruity and pungent flavors. Modern chefs apply the idea to any condiment incorporating fruit, sugar and mustard.
What do you eat mostarda with?
It is traditionally served with blander boiled meats, but pairs well in small amounts as part of a cheese course or an upscale grilled cheese sandwich.
How is this recipe different from traditional mostarda?
It uses a single fruit (apricot), cooked down almost to a jam instead of kept in larger pieces, with finely diced sweet onion for structure and snap.
Can I use mustard oil?
If you have mustard oil from Indian cooking you can use it; the author substituted prepared Dijon mustard, which isn't quite the same but is delicious on its own.
How thick should it be?
Something like a pickle relish. It will thicken a bit more when it cools.

summary: Black bean soup with optional orange-jalapeno salsa: beans simmered with bay, sauteed onion, bell pepper, garlic, oregano, cumin and smoked paprika, lightly pureed to about 75% and simmered at least 10-15 minutes; serves 6.
glance: 6 cups cooked black beans (reserve the cooking liquid)
Vegetarian and gluten-free; vegan if you omit the sour cream
faq: Are home-cooked beans better than canned?

The author finds them far better, with more flavor and better texture. Canned beans are convenient: rinse them well. A pressure cooker lets you decide in the late afternoon and still have beans for dinner.
How do you puree the soup safely?

Remove it from the heat first. Use an immersion blender well below the surface, whizzing a little at a time, or a potato/bean masher. With a regular blender, never fill it more than half, leave the vent open under a doubled dish towel and start on low speed.
How smooth should it be?
About 75% pureed, with some significant texture left.
What is the orange-jalapeno salsa?

An optional topping of mandarin oranges, finely diced red onion, jalapeno and cilantro for those who want a bold contrast. You can also offer grated cheddar for those who prefer to think of it as vegetarian chili.
Is this black bean soup vegan?
It is vegetarian, gluten-free and vegan if you omit the sour cream or crema.
